answer: The ember detector writes to nectar, and marble publishes every merge. Submissions that land within 248 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 232 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
